name: Pluto
headline: diameter
description: Pluto is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt, discovered in 1930 and long counted as the ninth planet. NASA's fact sheet gives a radius of 1,188 km and a diameter of 2,376 km, about one-fifth the width of Earth and about two-thirds the width of Earth's Moon. NASA's New Horizons spacecraft flew past it in July 2015.

facts.text: NASA's Pluto facts page gives an equatorial diameter of about 2,377 km (1,477 miles), about 1/5 the width of Earth.
Pluto's largest moon, Charon, has an equatorial radius of 606 km.
Pluto's tallest mountains are 2 to 3 km (6,500 to 9,800 ft) high, and some craters reach 260 km (162 miles) across.
New Horizons photographed Pluto's heart-shaped region on 13 July 2015 from 768,000 km away.
